thread.title: Integrating sustainability into infrastructure

author: TheManilaTimes
title: Integrating sustainability into infrastructure
text: Integrating sustainability into infrastructure **media[1295353]** ABOITIZ InfraCapital has successfully integrated its whole sustainability agenda across water utilities, airports and industrial estates, demonstrating how environmental management can be integrated into the development and operation of essential infrastructure. The infrastructure investment arm of the Aboitiz Group is pursuing initiatives focused on water security, emissions reduction, renewable energy, wastewater recycling and resource recovery as it seeks to balance business expansion with environmental responsibility. Its approach recognizes that infrastructure sustainability extends beyond constructing facilities with lower environmental footprints. It also involves managing natural resources, improving operational efficiency and building resilience into services that communities and businesses depend on. Water security is a major component of this strategy.Through Apo Agua Infrastructura, Aboitiz InfraCapital operates the Davao City Bulk Water Supply Project, which delivers more than 300 million liters of treated water daily to the Davao City Water District. The company has complemented its water infrastructure investments with watershed rehabilitation and riverbank restoration initiatives.These include a 50-hectare Adopt-a-Site project with the Davao City Water District, a 10-hectare riverbank restoration initiative with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources Region 11, and a 200-hectare rehabilitation site developed with DENR and the Farmers' Association for Rural Development Cooperative. The initiatives underscore the relationship between water infrastructure and the protection of natural ecosystems. Maintaining watersheds and river systems is essential to securing long-term water availability, particularly as climate change increases pressure on water resources.Advertisement Airport operations provide another important measure of the company's environmental commitments. Mactan-Cebu International Airport , operated by Aboitiz InfraCapital, achieved Airport Carbon Accreditation Level 2 – Reduction in August 2026. The recognition made it the first and only Philippine airport to attain that accreditation level at the time of its announcement. The airport's emissions-reduction measures include a 1.64-megawatt-peak rooftop solar installation, energy-efficient LED lighting, smart sensors and improvements in building management and heating, ventilation and air-conditioning systems.MCIA has also established a target of reducing emissions intensity by more than 90 percent by 2029 against its baseline, while pursuing net-zero carbon emissions by 2050. Advertisement These measures are particularly relevant to the aviation sector, where passenger growth and expanding airport operations create additional demands for electricity, fuel and other resources. Improving energy efficiency and incorporating renewable power can help reduce the environmental impact of airport expansion.At its industrial estates, Aboitiz InfraCapital is applying circular economy principles through initiatives that recover resources and reduce waste. LIMA Estate in Batangas launched its Sustainability Hub in March 2025, bringing together wastewater recycling, composting, materials recovery and plant propagation activities. Its greywater recycling facility reuses treated wastewater for non-potable applications, including irrigation. The facility has a storage capacity of 3.3 cubic meters.Advertisement The estate's composting facility can process up to one metric ton of food waste daily, producing approximately 100 kilograms of compost within 24 hours. Its plant nursery can produce approximately 15,000 propagates daily, supporting landscaping and green spaces within the industrial estate. The materials recovery facility further supports waste segregation and recovery, handling food, plastic, residual and hazardous waste streams.These initiatives illustrate how industrial estates can reduce their dependence on virgin resources while limiting the volume of waste sent to disposal facilities. The company has also explored converting plastic waste into green building materials, extending resource recovery beyond conventional recycling. Sustainability initiatives also extend to communities surrounding its infrastructure operations. Advertisement Among these is Solar Scholars, which provides solar-powered electricity to Pangan-an Elementary and High School in Lapu-Lapu City, supporting educational activities in an island community.The company's Elevate AIDA program, meanwhile, has provided women with digital skills training intended to improve access to employment opportunities. Coastal cleanup activities and environmental partnerships also form part of its community engagement efforts. Aboitiz InfraCapital is one of the 15 organizations vying for The Manila Times 2026 Sustainability Champions –\"Synergizing sustainability: Sectoral best practices\" on Nov. 20 at Marco Polo Hotel Ortigas.
summary: The infrastructure investment arm of the Aboitiz Group is pursuing initiatives focused on water security, emissions reduction, renewable energy, wastewater recycling and resource recovery as it seeks to balance business expansion with environmental responsibility. It also involves managing natural resources, improving operational efficiency and building resilience into services that communities and businesses depend on.
